One fundamental way we achieve this is by offering grants to organizations and individuals who share our dedication to improving the well-being of the elderly community. Application policies and guidelines The All Seniors Foundation is dedicated to enhancing the lives of senior citizens by supporting initiatives that align with our mission of providing high-quality care and services. Grant applications must be submitted by eligible organizations, including non-profits, community groups, and research institutions, that demonstrate a commitment to improving the well-being of seniors. Applicants are encouraged to design projects that address essential needs such as housing, wellness, technology, social engagement, and more. Applications should be clear, well-documented, and include a detailed plan that outlines the goals, benefits, and anticipated impact on senior communities. OAT provides telehealth funding and administers programs focused on direct services, research, and technical assistance. Which programs focus on technical assistance? Telehealth Resource Center Program Program Cycle: 9/1/2021 – 8/31/2025 The Telehealth Resource Centers (TRCs) deliver telehealth technical assistance. There are two types of HRSA Telehealth Resource Center (TRC) programs: Two National Telehealth Resource Center Programs (NTRC) focus on policy and technology. Twelve Regional Telehealth Resource Center Programs (RTRC) host activities and provide resources to rural and underserved areas. The HRSA Telehealth Resource Centers: Provide training and support Publicize information and research findings Support collaboration and partnerships Promote effective partnerships Promote the use of telehealth by providing health care information and education to the public and medical specialists The TRCs share expertise through individual consults, training, webinars, conference presentations, and the web. Waterville Community Fund Grant - Community Foundation of North Central Washington Skip to content LOGINS Fundholder Login Grant Applicant Login Scholarship Login Board Trustee Resources Local Advisory Board Login MENU Home About News & Events Giving Nonprofits Scholarships Professional Advisors Reserve a Conference Room WATERVILLE COMMUNITY FUND GRANT APPLY NOW Application Opens: October 1 Application Deadline: December 1 The Waterville Community Fund provides grant funding for innovative programs that help to meet the needs of the Waterville community and its citizens. The fund supports a variety of organizations and activities, such as: Arts and Culture Civic Projects Conservation and Environment Education Health and Human Services Priority is given to projects that provide enhancements to existing programs (rather than core operating needs,) have limited access to other funding sources, and that support the work of dedicated community volunteers. Grant Guidelines Applicants must be a 501(c)3 nonprofit charitable organization or governmental agency whose program serves the Waterville community. Grant funds must be expended within one year of award date. Grant funds must not be used to reimburse previously incurred expenses. Organizations are limited to one grant application per grant cycle (with the exception of those acting as a fiscal sponsor for another applicant). Evaluation Each application is reviewed by the Waterville Community Fund Advisory Committee with grant recommendations made to the Community Foundation’s Board of Trustees. Applicants will be notified of award status in December. Application Process – St. Louis City Senior Fund Skip to content St. Louis City Senior Fund Supporting an Aging-Friendly City About Us Grants Current Grantees Funding Opportunities Application Process Meetings & Reports News Contact Us Application Process Senior Fund only accepts applications when we have an open funding call; we do not accept applications on a rolling basis unless stated for a specific grant opportunity. To receive notices for new grant opportunities, sign up for our mailing list via the link on our Contact Us page. Contact our team anytime throughout the year if you would like to discuss a funding need for a program or service you provide. To apply for a Senior Fund grant, you must have an account in our grant application and management system called Grant Lifecycle Manager . Create an Online Account for Your Organization The first time your organization applies to one of our open funding opportunities, you will need to create an account with our secure online grants application management portal (also called Grant Lifecycle Manager or GLM). This tutorial from Foundant can assist with questions you have about getting started, or you can contact us with questions. If someone else from your organization has created an organizational account on our grant application site but you have not created your own individual user account yet, either someone with access to your Senior Fund account can add you or you can contact us. This tutorial from Foundant gives instructions on adding a user to your organization. You can also email us at our team email and we will provide you with individual login credentials to access your organization’s site. column3: Senior Fund Awards $3.01 Million in New Fund Defined Grants – St. Louis City Senior Fund Skip to content St. Louis City Senior Fund Supporting an Aging-Friendly City About Us Grants Current Grantees Funding Opportunities Application Process Meetings & Reports News Contact Us News Senior Fund Awards $3.01 Million in New Fund Defined Grants August 8, 2024 Stephanie Herbers Proposals from 15 organizations were approved by St. Louis City Senior Fund’s Board of Directors in May and June to receive a total of $3,010,232 for one-year and three-year grants that began July 1; $1 million in grant awards will be distributed during the fund’s current fiscal year (FY2025). The Fund Defined grant opportunity is funding awarded to address needs of older St. Louis City residents in specific focus areas determined by the Senior Fund Board of Directors based on community feedback and other sources. The Fund Defined awards that began their grant cycle in July focus on two areas: Housing and Economic Security. Organizations could apply for multi-year grants for up to three years. Senior Fund received 26 applications for this funding round for a total of $1.7 million in requests for the first year and $5.2 million in total for three years. The following organizations were awarded grants; 12 of the 15 grant awards supported continuation of services Senior Fund had supported in FY2022 – FY2024 (July 2021 – June 2024).
